Glossary

SB2 (official ballot town meeting)
Rindge holds town meeting in two parts. At the Deliberative Session voters discuss and can amend articles. A few weeks later everyone votes by ballot on the second Tuesday of March. RSA 40:13
Deliberative Session
The first session, held on a Saturday between the first and second Saturdays after the last Monday in January. Amendments are allowed, but they cannot remove an article's subject. RSA 40:13, III–IV
Warrant article
A question on the town ballot. The Select Board places most articles; 25 registered voters (or 2%, if fewer) can petition one onto the warrant. RSA 39:3
Default budget
The budget that applies if voters reject the operating budget: last year's appropriations, adjusted for debt service, contracts and legal obligations, minus one-time spending. Rindge went to default in 2011, 2021, 2025 and 2026. RSA 40:13, IX(b)
Capital reserve fund (CRF)
Money voters set aside for a future purchase, such as a truck or the revaluation. The fund's article says what it can be used for. Plain-language summary
ZBA (Zoning Board of Adjustment)
Five elected members serving 3-year terms. Hears appeals of zoning decisions and decides variances and special exceptions. Any action needs 3 concurring votes. Zoning Ord. Art. XV; RSA 674:33
Variance
ZBA permission to depart from the zoning ordinance. The applicant must meet all five tests: not contrary to the public interest, the ordinance's spirit is observed, substantial justice is done, surrounding values are not diminished, and enforcement would cause unnecessary hardship. Valid for 2 years unless used. RSA 674:33
Special exception
A use the ordinance allows only if the ZBA finds the listed conditions are met: no excessive traffic, noise or odors, no harm to nearby values, adequate septic, water and parking, and the town's attractiveness preserved. Zoning Ord. Art. XV.B
Frontage
The length of a lot along a public road maintained by the town or state, or in an approved subdivision, "to which the lot has legal right of access". Rindge requires 250 ft in every district. Zoning Ord. Art. XX #17
Class VI road
A public way the town does not maintain, including roads discontinued and made subject to gates and bars. RSA 229:5, VII
Conditional Use Permit
A Planning Board permit for uses the ordinance allows only under conditions, such as short-term rentals or home-based businesses in the Res-Ag district. Zoning Ord. Art. XII; RSA 674:21
3/5 vote
Bond articles need 60% yes, not a simple majority. Several Rindge articles have won a majority but still failed this test. As printed on Rindge bond ballots (see Trends)

Plain-language summaries, not legal advice. See the Laws section for sources.

Town facts and history

Rindge, incorporated in 1768, is a town of about 6,500 people with many lakes and ponds on the Massachusetts border.

In plain language

It covers about 40 square miles and had 6,476 residents in the 2020 Census.

Incorporated
1768 (Feb 11, 1768 per the Historical Society), named for Capt. Daniel Rindge of Portsmouth. Granted in 1736 by Massachusetts as "Rowley-Canada" and regranted in 1749 as "Monadnock No. 1". Official
Population
6,476 (2020 Census); 6,014 (2010); 6,502 estimated for July 1, 2025. The first census, in 1790, counted 1,143. NH Employment Security shows slightly different figures; the Census count is official. Official
Area
39.8 square miles: 37.1 land and 2.7 inland water. Elevation about 1,316 ft. ZIP 03461, area code 603, Cheshire County, on the Massachusetts border. Routes 119 and 202. Official
Villages and places
Rindge Center, Converseville, East Rindge, West Rindge, Cutter Hill, Jones Corner, Rand, Thomas, Woodmere. Official
Government
Select Board (3 members) and Town Administrator. SB2 official-ballot town meeting: Deliberative Session in late January or early February, vote on the second Tuesday of March (next: Tue Mar 9, 2027, derived). Official
Landmarks
Cathedral of the Pines; Franklin Pierce University; the Rindge Meeting House; Ingalls Memorial Library; Hillside and Meetinghouse cemeteries; the Town Common and gazebo. Official
Town histories
Stearns, History of Rindge, NH 1736–1874, and Town on the Border, Rindge 1874–1988 (box set $55 at the Town Office). Official
Historical Society museum
The town page names both the Hoyt-Allen house (c.1800–1840) and the Freeborn Stearns house (c.1815) for the museum (UNCONFIRMED which). OfficialUnconfirmed

Elderly exemption: current limits and how changes are made

Summary, not legal advice. Read the statutes and the town's figures at the linked sources, and confirm with the Town Clerk or Assessing Office.

Current Rindge elderly exemption (2025 Annual Report, MS-1 Elderly Exemption Report) OfficialConfirmed
AgeExemption from assessed valueRecipientsTotal granted
65–74$100,00020$1,876,600
75–79$140,00013$1,726,500
80+$200,00019$2,956,000
Total52$6,559,100
  • Income limits: $35,000 single, $49,000 married. Asset limits: $150,000 single, $150,000 married. The disabled exemption uses the same limits. OfficialConfirmed
  • The deadline to file for exemptions (elderly, disabled and others) was April 15, 2026, per the town calendar in the Annual Report. Official
  • These income limits were set by a March 2012 petition (Art 20, passed 615-492; digits read from a scan), which raised them from $25,000 single and $35,000 married. Official · scan, verify against PDF
  • The 2025 report prints the married income limit as $49,000; the 2020 report printed $50,000. Ask the Assessing Office which figure is current. OfficialUnconfirmed
  • March 2021, Art 19: the Deliberative Session amended a proposal to lower the limits into a committee to study it (18-6). The 748-376 vote was on that study article, and the exemption did not change. The annual report prints the original wording. Official · text-extracted · verify against PDF
  • March 2022, Art 11: a petition to lower the limits failed 395-601. Official
  • Recipients by year (MS-1 reports): 91 (2020), 92 (2021), 89 (2022), 88 (2023), 44 (2024) and 52 (2025). The drop followed the 2024 assessor review. Assessed value exempted was $11.07M in 2020 and $6.56M in 2025. Official
  • The 2026 warrant had no elderly-exemption article. No elderly or disabled exemption discussion was found in the 2026 agendas and minutes reviewed (175 documents) or in the Select Board meetings of Sept 9 to Oct 7. Official
  • The only related 2026 article was the veterans' disability tax credit increase to $4,500 (Article 12 on the final warrant; numbered Article 11 in the Jan 7 draft). It passed, per press reports. OfficialPress-reported

How exemptions are set under state law

  • RSA 72:39-b: towns set separate exemption amounts for ages 65–74, 75–79 and 80+. Minimums: income limits of at least $13,400 single / $20,400 married; asset limits of at least $35,000 (excluding the residence); each exemption at least $5,000. State law
  • RSA 72:39-a: "net income from all sources"; three consecutive years of NH residency before April 1; assets exclude the residence and up to the greater of 2 acres or the minimum lot size. State law
  • RSA 72:27-a: adopting or changing an exemption requires a town meeting vote, with the article placed on the warrant by the Select Board or by voter petition (RSA 39:3). The vote must state the exemption's provisions and amounts. State law

Petitioned warrant articles in general

  • RSA 39:3: a petitioned article needs the signatures of 25 registered voters or 2% of registered voters, whichever is less (never fewer than 10). The Select Board may make only minor textual changes. State law
  • Rindge is an SB2 town. Under RSA 40:13 II-a, petitions are due the second Tuesday in January: Tue Jan 12, 2027 (the preceding Friday, Jan 8, for bond articles). Statutory, not confirmed by the town
  • At the Deliberative Session, articles may be amended but not to eliminate their subject (RSA 40:13 IV(c)). State law

March 2027 zoning: wetlands setback, back lots, frontage, condominiums, Class VI roads

As of Oct 9, 2026, no amendment text or hearing notice has been posted. The Oct 6 Planning Board agenda lists "Possible Ordinance changes for March 2027 warrant" Official agenda · outcome not verified. Which amendments will go forward is not known.

Wetlands septic setback: 100 ft to 75 ft (under discussion)

  • Current rule (Wetlands Conservation District Ordinance, amended March 28, 2023): no septic tank or effluent disposal area for a new or expanded building within 100 ft of surface waters or vegetated wetlands; piping 50 ft. The 75 ft figure matches the State standard. Official
  • June 2 Planning Board: a Zoning Subcommittee member proposed meeting the Conservation Commission about changing the 100 ft setback. Official
  • June 8 Conservation Commission: concerns raised; under the current rule, builders can seek a ZBA variance below 100 ft. No vote. Official
  • July 23 Conservation Commission: $2,500 from the Conservation Fund for LEC Environmental Consultants to review the proposal, 5-0-1. OfficialTally from minutes text; verify against the PDF
  • Aug 10 Conservation Commission: report expected by 8/21, with a summary to the Select Board targeted for 9/1. No Commission vote or position on 75 ft appears in posted minutes. Official
  • An automated meeting summary says the Conservation Commission opposes the change and that a December hearing is planned. Neither is confirmed by an official record. Automated summary · unconfirmed
  • No article changing the setback from 100 ft to 75 ft has appeared on any Rindge ballot in the annual reports read (2011–2025). Official

Residential interior (back) lots

  • The March 2025 zoning ordinance has no interior-lot or flag-lot provision. Official
  • A subcommittee met March 16 and April 6. Ideas reported to the Planning Board on March 17: 300 ft frontage, no access across wetlands, owner occupancy of one lot. A draft was handed out April 7 and presented to the Conservation Commission June 8. No wording has been posted. The March 8, 2016 back-lot article failed 439-774, so a 2027 article would be a repeat attempt. Official

Frontage, condominiums, private and Class VI roads

  • Aug 4 Planning Board: listed as items to address. Not confirmed as warrant articles. OfficialUnconfirmed
  • The current minimum frontage is 250 ft, on a town- or state-maintained public right of way (or a Planning Board-approved subdivision) "to which the lot has legal right of access." Official
  • Frontage was the issue in five 2026 ZBA cases (2026-01, -06, -08, -09, -12). Official · draft minutes

Process and dates

  • Citizen zoning petitions: accepted Nov 9 to Dec 9, 2026 (RSA 675:4). Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by town
  • Planning Board hearings must be publicly noticed (RSA 675:7). Final hearing by Jan 25, 2027; the official copy goes to the Town Clerk by Feb 2, 2027. Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by town
  • 2025 precedent: the phasing-table amendment failed 757-805; the other zoning amendments passed. Official

March 2026 election

Voters turned down the proposed town budget in March 2026, so the $5,654,177 default budget applies.

In plain language

The proposed budget was $5.81 million and lost 707-824. All seven savings-fund articles passed. These results come from newspapers; the town has not posted official results.

The Deliberative Session was Sat Jan 31, 2026 Official and voting was Tue Mar 10, 2026 (7am–7pm, Rindge Memorial School). The town's results page returned an error on Oct 9, so the tallies are as reported by the Monadnock Ledger-Transcript and the Keene Sentinel, both re-checked online on Oct 9. They are not yet in any annual report.

The 100 ft septic setback from wetlands is a long-standing local rule. A switch to the state's 75 ft is being discussed, but no article with that change has ever been on a Rindge ballot.

First found
1986 (ordinance adopted)
Most recent
Aug 10, 2026 (ConCom minutes)
  1. Mar 11, 1986Wetlands Conservation District Ordinance adopted. Official
  2. Mar 2014Wetlands ordinance amendment passed narrowly, 746-705. Two petitioned wetlands articles (hazardous-material storage within 125 ft; storm-water runoff) passed 799-620 and 960-447. Official · scan, verify against PDF
  3. Mar 2023Wetlands ordinance rewrite passed 572-173 (the report dates the vote March 14, the ordinance cover says March 28). Official · text-extracted · verify against PDF
  4. Jun 2, 2026Planning Board subcommittee member proposes moving the 100 ft septic setback to the state's 75 ft. Official
  5. Jul 23, 2026Conservation Commission: $2,500 for LEC Environmental to review the change, 5-0-1. Official
  6. Fall 2026"Conservation Commission opposes" and "December hearing" appear only in an automated summary. Automated summary · unconfirmed
  7. 2011–2025No 100 ft to 75 ft article appears in any annual report. A March 2027 article would be the first. Official

            Rindge by the numbers

            The key figures, including the 2025 tax rate of $13.79 per $1,000 and the elderly exemption count.

            In plain language

            About 6,500 people live in Rindge. After the 2025 revaluation the tax rate fell to $13.79 per $1,000, because assessed values roughly doubled. That does not mean tax bills were cut in half.

            Budget and finances

            The town spends about $5.5 to $5.8 million a year on its own operations, before school and county taxes.

            In plain language

            Voters rejected the proposed budget in 2025 and 2026, so the default budget applies. The largest lines are police, highway and fire.

            Department budgets, savings funds, debt and the capital plan, from the town's 2024 and 2025 annual reports. 2026 vote results are press-reported.

            Read this first

            • The 2025 and 2024 tax rates ($13.79 and $25.31) are not comparable. The 2025 revaluation roughly doubled assessed values (net valuation $1,466,136,314), so the rate per $1,000 fell. It does not mean bills were cut in half. Official
            • 2025 gross appropriations of $6,134,500 appear on the tax-rate calculation page, but the figure is from a scan and uncertain. Official · scan, verify against PDF
            • 2026 vote results are press-reported (Monadnock Ledger-Transcript, Mar 11, 2026). The town's results sheet was not located. Press-reported
            • The 2023 and 2024 annual reports both print 497-256 for the operating budget. Both are withheld pending a check of the ballots. Withheld: suspect duplicate tally

            Debt and the fiber bond

            • 2020 fiber-to-the-premises bond: total project $5,037,825, of which $2,579,125 was bonded and the rest contributed by Consolidated Communications. Passed 1,151-174. Bond proceeds received Aug 13, 2020. Official
            • Debt service in the budget: $130,000 principal and $40,363 interest in 2025; the same amounts in the 2026 default budget. Official
            • The $130,000 a year of principal appears to be for the 2020 fiber bond. The annual reports do not say so; this is an inference. Inference, not stated by the town
            • The town receives $186,000 a year from Consolidated Communications (CCI Fiber) and held $742,847 in the CCI Fiber account at the end of 2025. Official
            • 2025 Art 11, to spend $60,375 of unused bond proceeds on the Town Office HVAC, failed 576-1,045 (needed 3/5). Official

            Capital Improvement Program (CIP)

            • Fall 2025 CIP recommendations for the 2026 warrant: Fire $150,000; Highway $165,000; facilities $35,000; Recreation $50,000; Library $20,000; Meetinghouse $25,000 (total $445,000). The warrant that went to voters: Highway $185,000, Fire $125,000, Building $35,000, Recreation $25,000, Library $20,000, Meetinghouse $25,000. Official
            • 2024 CIP recommendations for the 2025 warrant totaled $565,000. In March 2025 the Fire, Highway, Building, Police and Meetinghouse articles failed; Revaluation, Library and Recreation passed. Official

            Not found

            • A schedule of long-term debt (outstanding principal, interest rate, maturity) is not printed in any 2011–2025 annual report. Gap
            • The 2026 tax rate has not been set or found. Gap
            • No multi-year Capital Improvement Program table was found online; only yearly committee recommendations. Gap
            • The school district budget is not in the town report (see Schools and community). Gap
            • A FY2027 draft town budget was not found. Gap

            Laws and rules

            Zoning, regulations and the state laws behind them, in plain language.

            • Laws and regulations
            1. Home
            2. Laws and rules

            Laws and regulations that apply in Rindge

            Plain-language notes on Rindge's zoning, its regulations and the state laws behind them, each linked to the official text.

            In plain language

            Rindge's zoning ordinance sets lot sizes, setbacks and frontage (250 feet on a public road in the residential and village districts). State law sets how rules change: zoning changes and citizen petitions go to voters on the March ballot. This is a summary, not legal advice.

            Summary, not legal advice. These plain-language notes point to the official text. Laws change; read the linked source and check with the Planning Department, Town Clerk or a lawyer before acting.

            How a zoning change becomes law

            1. 1
              Idea

              The Planning Board drafts an amendment, or 25+ voters petition one (RSA 675:4).

              Petitions accepted Nov 9 – Dec 9, 2026 Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by townUnconfirmed

            2. 2
              Public hearing

              The Planning Board holds at least one hearing, with 10 calendar days' notice (RSA 675:3, 675:7).

              Final hearing by Jan 25, 2027 Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by townUnconfirmed

            3. 3
              Revise?

              A substantive change needs another hearing at least 14 days later (RSA 675:3).

            4. 4
              On file

              The final text goes to the Town Clerk by the fifth Tuesday before the vote (RSA 675:3, V).

              Feb 2, 2027 Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by townUnconfirmed

            5. 5
              Ballot

              Voters decide by simple majority, or 2/3 if a valid protest petition is filed (RSA 675:5).

              Tue Mar 9, 2027 Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by townUnconfirmed

            6. 6
              Law

              Takes effect on passage (Zoning Ord. Art. XIX). Projects already approved may be protected (RSA 674:39).

            How a citizen petition works

            1. 1
              Write it

              Draft the question in warrant-article form. The Select Board may make only minor wording changes.

            2. 2
              Signatures

              25 registered voters, or 2% of the checklist if fewer, and never fewer than 10 (RSA 39:3).

            3. 3
              Submit

              To the Select Board by the second Tuesday in January (RSA 40:13, II-a).

              Tue Jan 12, 2027 (Fri Jan 8 for bonds) Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by townUnconfirmed

            4. 4
              Warrant

              The article is placed on the posted warrant.

              Warrant posted by Jan 25, 2027 Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by townUnconfirmed

            5. 5
              Deliberative Session

              Voters may amend it but cannot remove its subject (RSA 40:13, IV).

              Sat Jan 30 – Feb 6, 2027 Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by townUnconfirmed

            6. 6
              Ballot

              Simple majority (3/5 for bonds). Exemption changes take effect the next April 1 (RSA 72:27-a).

              Tue Mar 9, 2027 Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by townUnconfirmed

            Dates are computed from state law for a Tue Mar 9, 2027 vote. They are statutory-derived and unconfirmed by the town for 2027, so check them with the Town Clerk.

            Showing all 68 entries

            Local · Zoning Ordinance (amended Mar 11, 2025)

            • Local

              Art. I: Preamble

              Adopted March 14, 1961 under RSA 672–677. Ten separate ordinances are part of the zoning ordinance: Sign, Wetland Conservation District, Phased Development, Aquifer Protection, Underground Storage Tank, Floodplain, Sexually Oriented Business, Wireless Telecommunication, Accessory Dwelling Unit and Small Wind Energy.

              What it means for Rindge: All of these are enforced as zoning, and changing any of them takes a ballot vote.

              Official Source for Art. I: Preamble (opens in new tab)

            • Local

              Art. II: Districts

              Eight districts: Residential, Residential-Agricultural, Village, College, Business-Light Industry, Commercial, Gateway Central and Gateway East, shown on the zoning map dated Sept 9, 2008.

              What it means for Rindge: The town posts a "2025 Zoning Map", but the article still cites the 2008 date (an open question for the Planning Department).

              Official Source for Art. II: Districts (opens in new tab)

            • Local

              Art. III: General provisions

              Applies everywhere. Any use not listed is prohibited (added 2025, 999-611). Building permits are required, and the State Building Code applies (2023). No building within 50 ft of the high-water line of a water body (III.G.4). Height limit 45 ft (III.L). Road acceptance goes through a Roadway Committee (III.K). Rules for home occupations (III.J) and campers (III.N).

              What it means for Rindge: Check here first before building or changing a use.

              Official Source for Art. III: General provisions (opens in new tab)

            • Local

              Art. III.I: Planned Unit Residential Development (PURD)

              The Planning Board may vary density and frontage in a PURD. Overall density cannot exceed one unit per minimum lot size; ADUs added later are exempt from the density limit (2024). Allowed in the Residential, Res-Ag, Village and College districts.

              What it means for Rindge: This is how cluster subdivisions such as Saybrook were approved.

              Official Source for Art. III.I: Planned Unit Residential Development (PURD) (opens in new tab)

            • Local

              Art. III.S: Short-term rentals

              Renting all or part of a dwelling for less than 30 days needs Site Plan approval and a Planning Board Conditional Use Permit. Occupancy is limited to 3 people per bedroom, and septic, water, parking and life safety are reviewed.

              What it means for Rindge: In effect since the March 11, 2025 vote (881-717). Before that, rentals were a permitted accessory use with parking rules only.

              Official Source for Art. III.S: Short-term rentals (opens in new tab)

            • Local

              Arts. IV–XI: District rules

              Residential (IV): single-family only. Res-Ag (V): farms and one- or two-family homes, with multi-family by special exception. Village (VI): adds small offices and shops with site plan review. College (VII): adds college uses. Commercial (VIII): no fuel or vehicle sales. Business-Light Industry (IX): adds vehicles, manufacturing and trucking. Gateway Central and East (X–XI): mixed use on Routes 119 and 202, with 30% open space.

              What it means for Rindge: See the dimensional table below for frontage, lot size and setbacks.

              Official Source for Arts. IV–XI: District rules (opens in new tab)

            • Local

              Art. XII: Conditional Use Permits

              The applicant must show the use conforms to area and setback rules and the Master Plan, keeps the ordinance's spirit, does not harm health or safety, causes no excessive noise or loss of nearby values, and "will not adversely affect wetlands or the ground water resources".

              What it means for Rindge: Used for short-term rentals, home-based businesses (Res-Ag) and motor vehicle repair (Gateway East).

              Official Source for Art. XII: Conditional Use Permits (opens in new tab)

            • Local

              Art. XIII: Nonconforming uses and lots (incl. XIII.E)

              A nonconforming use stopped for a year must then conform. Expanding a nonconforming building needs a ZBA special exception. XIII.E: a lot of record that is too small for current frontage or area rules can still hold one single-family home, but setbacks apply.

              What it means for Rindge: Covers many older Rindge lots. Voters deleted the forced-merger rules in 2015 (864-307 and 828-334).

              Official Source for Art. XIII: Nonconforming uses and lots (incl. XIII.E) (opens in new tab)

            • Local

              Art. XV: Board of Adjustment, special exceptions and variances

              Five elected members. XV.B sets the special-exception test. XV.C lets the ZBA grant variances when the applicant meets all the criteria required by law (RSA 674:33).

              What it means for Rindge: Frontage shortfalls are the most common reason Rindge owners go to the ZBA.

              Official Source for Art. XV: Board of Adjustment, special exceptions and variances (opens in new tab)

            • Local

              Arts. XIV, XVI–XIX: Enforcement, amendment, penalty

              The Select Board enforces (RSA 676:15–19). Amendments are made by town meeting vote (RSA 675:3), penalties follow RSA 676:17, and amendments take effect on passage.

              What it means for Rindge: Changes adopted in March take effect right away.

              Official Source for Arts. XIV, XVI–XIX: Enforcement, amendment, penalty (opens in new tab)

            • Local

              Art. XX: Definitions

              36 definitions. #17 Frontage: "The uninterrupted length of a lot bordering a public right of way maintained by the town or state, or in a subdivision approved by the Planning Board, to which the lot has legal right of access." #21 Lot of record, #14 Multi-unit (3–6 units), #31 Short-term rental (under 30 days). No definition of back lot, interior lot, flag lot or condominium.

              What it means for Rindge: The Planning Board has listed the frontage definition for review (Aug 4, 2026).

              Official Source for Art. XX: Definitions (opens in new tab)

            Local · Other ordinances (voted at town meeting)

            • Local

              Wetlands Conservation District Ordinance

              Covers surface waters and wetlands, with minimal-disturbance zones of 150 ft around surface waters and 50 ft around vegetated wetlands over 3,000 sq ft. No building or impervious surface within 50 ft (§5.A). No new septic system within 100 ft (§5.B); piping 50 ft. Hazardous materials 125 ft, salt storage and snow dumping 250 ft. The Conservation Commission gets notice of applications.

              What it means for Rindge: The 100 ft septic setback is the rule discussed for a possible change to 75 ft. No such article has appeared on any ballot to date. Amended 2014 and 2023.

              Official Source for Wetlands Conservation District Ordinance (opens in new tab)

              Accessory Dwelling Unit Ordinance (Mar 10, 2026)

              One ADU per home, attached or detached, by right, in the Residential, Res-Ag, Village and College districts and on legal non-conforming single-family lots elsewhere. The owner lives in one of the units. 300 to 950 sq ft (or one third of the main home's floor area if the home is 2,850 sq ft or more). One parking space per unit, and the septic must be certified.

              What it means for Rindge: Brought into line with RSA 674:72 by the March 2026 vote (1,130-526, press).

            State · Zoning powers and boards

            • State

              RSA 672:1 and 672:3: Purpose; who is an abutter

              Land-use regulation is a local responsibility within state limits. An abutter is anyone whose NH property adjoins, or is directly across the street or stream from, the land under review.

              What it means for Rindge: Abutters get notice of Rindge Planning Board and ZBA hearings and can appeal.

              State law Source for RSA 672:1 and 672:3: Purpose; who is an abutter (opens in new tab)

            • State

              RSA 673:1 and 673:3, V: Boards; dual-member recusal

              Town meeting may create a planning board. Since 2025, a person on both the ZBA and the Planning Board must not vote at the ZBA on a matter they voted on at the Planning Board.

              What it means for Rindge: Applies if any Rindge member sits on both boards.

              State law Source for RSA 673:1 and 673:3, V: Boards; dual-member recusal (opens in new tab)

            • State

              RSA 674:16–19: Zoning power, purposes, existing uses

              Only town meeting can adopt or amend zoning. Zoning must serve listed purposes such as health, safety and preventing overcrowding. It does not apply to existing structures and uses, though it can apply to substantial changes.

              What it means for Rindge: Every Rindge zoning change, including the wetlands and back-lot ideas, must pass at the ballot.

              State law Source for RSA 674:16–19: Zoning power, purposes, existing uses (opens in new tab)

            • State

              RSA 674:16, VII–VIII: Parking cap and occupancy floor (2025)

              Towns cannot require more than one residential parking space per unit, or limit occupancy below 2 people per bedroom.

              What it means for Rindge: Local rules that are stricter are overridden.

              State law Source for RSA 674:16, VII–VIII: Parking cap and occupancy floor (2025) (opens in new tab)

            State · Housing and ADUs

            • State

              RSA 674:58–59: Workforce housing

              Every town's land-use rules must give "reasonable and realistic opportunities" for workforce housing, including rental multi-family housing.

              What it means for Rindge: Applies to Rindge's ordinance as a whole.

              State law Source for RSA 674:58–59: Workforce housing (opens in new tab)

            • State

              RSA 674:71–73: Accessory dwelling units

              Towns must allow one ADU, attached or detached, by right wherever single-family homes are allowed. The size cap is 950 sq ft unless the town allows more, and a town cannot set it below 750 sq ft. A town may require the owner to live in one unit but cannot say which. Existing structures such as garages can be converted even if their setbacks are nonconforming. Amended 2025 and 2026 (effective Aug 31, 2026).

              What it means for Rindge: Rindge updated its ADU ordinance to match in March 2026.

              State law Source for RSA 674:71–73: Accessory dwelling units (opens in new tab)

            • State

              RSA 674:79–81: Multi-family on commercial land; child care

              Per state and association summaries, from July 1, 2026 towns must allow multi-family housing on commercial land where roads, water and sewer are adequate, and must allow licensed child care centers by right in commercial zones. The statute pages were not checked.

              What it means for Rindge: Rindge's commercial districts may need updates; status unverified.

              State / association summary, not the statuteUnconfirmed Source for RSA 674:79–81: Multi-family on commercial land; child care (opens in new tab)

            State · Roads and frontage

            • State

              RSA 674:41: Building permits and road access (Class VI, private roads)

              A building permit generally needs access from a Class V or better road, a road on an approved plat, a Class VI road with a recorded liability waiver and other statutory conditions, or a private road meeting the statute's conditions. The 2025 changes (SB 281, HB 296) are in the current text; the State planning office gives July 1, 2026 as the Class VI effective date.

              What it means for Rindge: Rindge's 250 ft frontage rule can still require a ZBA variance. Ask the Building Department before buying or building on a Class VI road.

              Class VI roads are public ways the town does not maintain, including roads discontinued subject to gates and bars. The town still has the same regulatory authority over them as over Class V roads.

              What it means for Rindge: Explains what "Class VI" means in Rindge discussions.

              Only a town vote can discontinue a road or make it subject to gates and bars, with notice to abutters at least 14 days before the vote.

              An approved plat or site plan is exempt from later zoning and regulation changes for 7 years if active and substantial development starts within 3 years (approvals on or after July 1, 2023).

Paragraph IX(b) defines the default budget, and paragraph II-a sets the deadlines, including petitions due the second Tuesday in January.

            How do I...?

            Step-by-step help with common tasks, from permits and licenses to property tax bills.

            In plain language

            Guides cover permits, dog licenses, registering a vehicle, voting, and appealing or lowering a property tax bill. Each one says who to contact and what to check first.

            • How do I get a building permit?

              Steps

              1. Check zoning first: district, setbacks, frontage and wetlands. For anything beyond a simple house, call Planning (x117). A permit is required before any building goes up (Zoning Art. III.A).
              2. Get the right form from the Building Department documents page. Attach plans and pay the fee with the application; inspections are not scheduled until payment is in.
              3. Applications are reviewed every Wednesday at 10 am.
              4. Request each inspection at least 24 hours ahead by phone or text to (603) 969-3354. Do not request inspections by email.
              5. Get a certificate of occupancy before moving in or changing use, including seasonal to year-round (Zoning Art. III.C).

              Fees (2026 schedule, scanned; verify before quoting). Minimum $60. New one- or two-family home $0.40 per sq ft of living area; basements, garages, decks and porches $0.25 per sq ft. Additions $0.40 per sq ft. Demolition $65. Pools $60. Starting work without a permit doubles the fee, and violations can cost $100 a day.

              Single-family homes. Single-family homes and duplexes do not need Planning Board site plan review.

              Who handles it. Building Department, (603) 899-5181 x109, buildingdept@rindgenh.gov.

              Legal basis. Zoning Ordinance Art. III.A and III.C; NH State Building Code (RSA 155-A).

              OfficialOfficial · scan, verify against PDF Building forms page (opens in new tab) · 2026 permit fee schedule (opens in new tab) · Zoning Ordinance (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • The fee schedule says permits are valid 1 year in one place and 180 days in another. Ask the Building Department.
              • No online permit portal was found (unconfirmed).

            • How do I get a driveway permit?

              Steps

              1. Get the Residential (or Commercial) Driveway Access Permit Application from the Planning Board applications page.
              2. Check the Driveway Regulations: residential driveways 10–20 ft wide; sight distance by road speed (150 ft at 25 mph up to 400 ft at 60 mph); runoff must not enter the road.
              3. Attach a sketch plan. A rough drawing is accepted.
              4. Pay two checks to the Town of Rindge: a $50 application fee and a $500 security bond, which may be returned once the driveway passes.
              5. Public Works inspects before approval and before construction starts.

              Class VI or private road. Building on a Class VI or private road needs a Class VI Road Waiver (RSA 674:41). The fee is $50 total, in two checks: $12.78 to the Cheshire County Registry of Deeds and $37.22 to the Town.

              Who handles it. Planning Department (x117); inspection by Public Works.

              Legal basis. RSA 236:13; Zoning Art. III.A.2; Driveway Regulations (amended Dec 5, 2017).

              Official Planning Board applications (opens in new tab) · Driveway Regulations (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • The form is dated 2012. Ask Planning whether the $50 and $500 amounts are current.
              • State highways need a NH DOT driveway permit (not researched).

            • How do I put in a septic system or work near wetlands?

              Steps

              1. A licensed NH septic designer prepares the plan. NH DES must approve construction before you build, and approve operation before use.
              2. Rindge's Wetlands Conservation District Ordinance: a new septic tank or leach field must be at least 100 ft from surface waters and vegetated wetlands; septic piping at least 50 ft. No building or pavement within 50 ft. No fertilizer (other than limestone) within 25 ft.
              3. Work in wetlands or streams usually needs a NH DES wetlands permit. Land within 250 ft of public waters is protected shoreland.
              4. Talk to the Planning Department early. The Conservation Commission gets notice of applications affecting the wetlands district.

              Pending change. The Planning Board has discussed changing the septic setback from 100 ft to 75 ft for the March 2027 ballot. No amendment text was posted as of Oct 9, 2026, so 100 ft is the rule today.

              Who handles it. NH DES, (603) 271-3503; locally Planning (x117) and Code Enforcement (x115).

              Legal basis. RSA 482-A, 483-B, 485-A; Rindge Wetlands Ordinance.

              Official Wetlands Ordinance (amended March 28, 2023) (opens in new tab) · NH DES septic systems (opens in new tab) · NH DES wetlands permit help (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • Ordinance date conflict: the Annual Report says the vote was March 14, 2023; the ordinance cover says March 28, 2023.
              • DES fees were not collected.

            • How do I rent my home short-term (under 30 days)?

              Steps

              1. Short-term rentals need Site Plan approval and a Conditional Use Permit from the Planning Board.
              2. Applications are due at the Planning Department at least 21 days before the hearing. The Board hears applications at its first meeting of the month.
              3. The Board looks at septic, water, parking, occupancy (up to 3 people per bedroom) and life-safety inspections.

              When adopted. March 11, 2025, 881-717 (Zoning Art. III.S and Art. XII).

              Who handles it. Planning Department (x117).

              Legal basis. Zoning Ordinance Art. III.S and XII; RSA 674:21.

              Official Planning Board applications (opens in new tab) · Zoning Ordinance (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • Application fees were not extracted.
              • No separate STR registration or fee was found.

            • How do I add an accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?

              Steps

              1. One ADU per lot, attached or detached, in the Residential, Residential-Agricultural, Village and College districts, and on legal non-conforming single-family lots elsewhere.
              2. The owner lives in either unit. Size: at least 300 sq ft; at most 950 sq ft (or one-third of a larger home). Two exits, interconnected fire alarms, parking, and a septic system certified adequate.
              3. Get a building permit; plans must show the ADU area. There is no separate ADU form.

              State law. RSA 674:71–73 limits what towns can require. A town may require owner occupancy of one unit but cannot say which.

              Who handles it. Building Department (permit); Planning (x117) for questions.

              Legal basis. Rindge ADU Ordinance (2026); RSA 674:71–73.

              Official ADU Ordinance (2026) (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • The 2026 state amendment (effective Aug 31, 2026) was not compared line by line with the town ordinance. Confirm with Planning.

            • How do I put up a sign?

              Steps

              1. Most signs need a permit before they go up or change. Some temporary, charitable and construction signs are exempt but must still meet district rules.
              2. Apply to the Select Board or its designee with location, size, lighting, materials and a drawing, signed by the business and property owners.
              3. Permits carry an annual renewal fee due April 30.

              Who handles it. Select Board office; enforcement by Code Enforcement (x115).

              Legal basis. Sign Ordinance (amended March 12, 2024).

              Official Sign Ordinance (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • No sign permit form or fee amount was found on the website.

            • How do I get a burn permit?

              Steps

              1. New Hampshire requires a written fire permit for open burning unless the ground is snow-covered. Ask the Rindge Fire Department.
              2. Allowed: untreated wood and brush up to 5 inches across. Not allowed: household trash, construction debris, treated wood.
              3. Check fire danger the same day.

              Penalty (2026 fee schedule, scanned). Unauthorized burning can bring a state warning and a $350 town fee.

              Who handles it. Fire Department, (603) 899-3324, rfdchief@rindgenh.gov.

              Legal basis. RSA 227-L; Res 5600; Env-A 1000.

              OfficialOfficial · scan, verify against PDF NH Forest Protection: fire permits (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • Rindge's local permit hours and process are not posted. Whether Rindge uses NHFirePermit.com is unconfirmed (the site returned an error).

            • How do I license my dog?

              Steps

              1. License every dog with the Town Clerk's office by April 30 each year. New tags go on sale in January.
              2. Renew online through the town's online payments if not late, or in person at the Town Offices.
              3. Bring proof of rabies vaccination (confirm with the office).

              Fees. $7.50 spayed or neutered; $10.00 not; $2.00 for one dog owned by a senior (65+); $20.00 group license for 5 or more dogs.

              Who handles it. Town Clerk's office, (603) 899-5181 x107.

              Legal basis. RSA 466 (not fetched; the town page is the source).

              Official Town Clerk page (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • Late-license penalty not found.

            • How do I register a vehicle?

              Steps

              1. Register with the town first; the Town Clerk's office collects the town permit fee and the state fee together.
              2. Renew online with E-Reg or in person.
              3. Moving to Rindge: bring your documents and the address-change form to the Town Clerk's office.

              State fees (from Dec 31, 2025). Title $35. Passenger vehicles up to 3,000 lb $42 a year; 3,001–5,000 lb $48; 5,001–8,000 lb $66. Motorcycles $30. Vanity plates $60 a year.

              Who handles it. Town Clerk's office, (603) 899-5181 x107.

              Legal basis. RSA 261; RSA 261:153 (town permit fee).

              Official Motor vehicles page (opens in new tab) · E-Reg online renewal (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • The town permit-fee rate table is not on the town page.

            • How do I register to vote or vote absentee?

              Steps

              1. You can vote if you are a U.S. citizen, 18 or older on election day, and live in Rindge.
              2. Register at the Town Clerk's office, at the Supervisors of the Checklist session (Wed Oct 28, 2026, the posted deadline before the Nov 3 election), or at the polls on election day.
              3. Bring proof of citizenship, age, domicile and identity.
              4. Absentee: request a form from the Town Clerk's office. Deadlines: by mail, noon the day before the election; in person, 5 pm the day before (Mon Nov 2 for the Nov 3 election).

              Where to vote. Rindge Memorial School Gymnasium, 58 School Street, 7 am–7 pm.

              Who handles it. Town Clerk's office, (603) 899-5181 x107; Supervisors of the Checklist.

              Legal basis. RSA 654:12; RSA 657.

              Official Voter registration (opens in new tab) · NH Secretary of State: register to vote (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • The town elections pages say they are under construction. The 2026 town absentee form must be replaced by a 2027 version.

            • How do I appeal my property assessment (abatement)?

              Steps

              1. Pay your bill on time. An abatement request does not stop the tax from being due.
              2. File the abatement application by March 1 after the final bill (for 2026 bills: March 1, 2027).
              3. Give specific reasons, such as a factual error or a value out of line with similar properties. Include photos or comparable sales.
              4. The town must answer in writing by July 1. No answer means denial.
              5. If denied, appeal by September 1 to the NH Board of Tax and Land Appeals ($65 fee per the town page) or Superior Court.

              Who handles it. Assessing, (603) 899-5181 x113; the Select Board decides.

              Legal basis. RSA 76:16; RSA 76:16-a.

              Official The abatement process (opens in new tab) · RSA 76:16 (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • Confirm which form year to use (the abatement page links a 2025 form).

            • How do I apply for a tax exemption or credit?

              Steps

              1. File form PA-29 with Assessing between the December tax bill and April 15. Attach the worksheet or documents (DD-214 for veterans).
              2. Approvals are permanent; the town sends a renewal form every 5 years.
              3. Elderly (65+): $100,000 off assessed value at 65–74, $140,000 at 75–79, $200,000 at 80+. Income under $35,000 single or $49,000 married; assets under $150,000 (not counting the home).
              4. Veterans: $500 credit; surviving spouse $700; service-connected total disability $4,500 (raised by 2026 Art. 12, press-reported).

              Other. Disabled exemption $100,000 (same limits as elderly). Blind $15,000. Solar exemption available. Current use: file form A-10 by April 15.

              State relief. Low and moderate income homeowners can apply to NH DRA between May 1 and June 30.

              Who handles it. Assessing, (603) 899-5181 x113.

              Legal basis. RSA 72:27-a, 72:39-a/b, 72:28, 72:35, 72:62, 79-A.

              Official Exemptions and credits (opens in new tab) · Assessing forms (opens in new tab)

              Check first:
              • The 2020 report printed a $50,000 married income limit; the 2025 report says $49,000.
              • Residency rules differ between the town page (1 year for veterans) and the worksheet (3 or 5 years).

            • How do I file a citizen petition for the March ballot?

              Steps

              1. Get 25 registered Rindge voters to sign (RSA 39:3).
              2. Submit it to the Select Board by the second Tuesday in January: Jan 12, 2027 (derived from statute; confirm with the town).
              3. Zoning petitions have an earlier window: Nov 9 – Dec 9, 2026 (derived).

              Step-by-step. See the flow diagrams in the Laws section.

              Who handles it. Select Board office, (603) 899-5181 x101.

              Legal basis. RSA 39:3; RSA 40:13; RSA 675:4.

              Derived from statute / NHMA calendar · not posted by townUnconfirmed How a citizen petition works

            • How do I go to or watch a meeting?

              Steps

              1. Select Board: usually every other Wednesday, 6 pm, Town Offices Conference Room. Planning Board: 1st and 3rd Tuesday, 7 pm. ZBA: 4th Tuesday, 7 pm.
              2. Meetings are open to the public. Agendas are posted on each board's page.
              3. Select Board meetings stream on Town Hall Streams.

              Who handles it. Select Board office, (603) 899-5181 x100.

              Legal basis. RSA 91-A (open meetings).

              Official Town Hall Streams (opens in new tab) · Select Board agendas and minutes (opens in new tab)

              Check first:

            • How do I sign up for emergency alerts?

              Steps

              1. Rindge is moving to NH Alerts (the state system, powered by Genasys Protect).
              2. Register on the state Genasys portal for calls, texts and email, or use the free Genasys Protect app.
              3. For town news by email, sign up for eNotify.

              Who handles it. Fire Department / Emergency Management, (603) 899-3324.

            Emergency and utilities

            In an emergency, call 911.

            In plain language

            Ambulance service is due to switch to Peterborough Fire & Rescue on January 1, 2027 (press-reported). No town water or sewer system is listed, so homes generally use private wells and septic (unconfirmed).

            911

            Police, fire or medical emergency. Call or text 911.

            Emergency services

            • Emergency. Dial 911 for police, fire or medical emergencies. Official
            • Police, non-emergency. (603) 899-5009, Mon–Fri 8–4. After hours (603) 355-2000. 158 Main Street. Official Source (opens in new tab)
            • Fire Department. (603) 899-3324, 150 Main Street. The Fire Chief is also the Emergency Management Director. Official Source (opens in new tab)
            • Ambulance. Jaffrey-Rindge Memorial Ambulance serves Rindge through Dec 31, 2026. Peterborough Fire & Rescue takes over Jan 1, 2027 (Select Board vote 2-0-1, Sept 9, 2026, press-reported; the contract is subject to voter approval). Press-reported Source (opens in new tab)
            • Alerts. Rindge is moving to NH Alerts (Genasys Protect). Register on the state portal or use the free app. Town news by email: eNotify. Official Source (opens in new tab)
            • Shelters and warming centers. The 2019 emergency plan lists the Recreation Department and Rindge Memorial School as mass-care resources. No currently designated shelter or warming center is confirmed (UNCONFIRMED). The town is updating its emergency plan. OfficialUnconfirmed
            • Non-emergency help. Dial 211 for statewide help lines. Official
            • Roads and snow. Public Works, (603) 899-2105. The snow and ice policy is available at the Town Office. Official Source (opens in new tab)
            • Health Officer. (603) 899-5181 x100. Official Source (opens in new tab)

            Utilities

            • Electricity. Eversource is the utility. Residents can opt in to Community Power (Community Power Coalition of NH). The Energy Commission page cites $0.086/kWh versus Eversource's $0.10403 default, with no date; check current rates. OfficialStale town page · check with the office Source (opens in new tab)
            • Water and sewer. No municipal water or sewer system is listed for Rindge, consistent with private wells and septic systems (UNCONFIRMED; ask the Town Office or NH DES). Unconfirmed
            • Trash and recycling. Transfer station, 113 Main Street: Tue 10–7, Thu 10–7, Fri 1–7, Sat 8–3. Stickers $50 ($25 for one senior per household), sold at the Town Clerk's or Selectmen's office. No town curbside pickup confirmed (UNCONFIRMED). Official Source (opens in new tab)
            • Broadband. A town-owned fiber network built in 2020–21 with Consolidated Communications (marketed as Fidium Fiber), financed by a ~$2.6M bond repaid from capped subscriber fees, not taxes, per press reports. The town receives $186,000 a year. Press-reported Source (opens in new tab)

            Schools and community

            Rindge children attend the Jaffrey-Rindge Cooperative School District (SAU 47), whose budget is voted separately from the town's.

            In plain language

            Rindge Memorial School serves PreK–5, then students go to Conant Middle and High School in Jaffrey.

            Jaffrey-Rindge Cooperative School District (SAU 47) Official

            1 Conant Way, Jaffrey, NH 03452 · (603) 532-8122 · sau47.org (opens in new tab)

            The School Board meets the 1st and 3rd Monday, public session 6:30 pm unless the agenda says otherwise. Agendas usually post the Thursday or Friday before; videos the same week.

            Schools serving Rindge (NH DOE); enrollment 2024–25 (NCES)

            (603) 899-3363            		324

            2023–24 enrollment differed (Rindge Memorial 319, Conant High 368, Conant Middle 257). Franklin Pierce University, Hampshire Country School and Heritage Christian School are also listed by the town.

            Recent school votes Press-reported

            • March 2025: a $22.9M career and technical education (CTE) expansion was defeated; Rindge voted 1,074-611 against. Source (opens in new tab)
            • March 2025: the $30.76M school budget passed after a $3M cut; Rindge voted 1,011-682 in favor. Source (opens in new tab)
            • March 2026: the $33.5M school budget failed districtwide by 68 votes; Rindge voted 943-608 against. Source (opens in new tab)

            School budgets are voted separately from the town budget and are not in the town's annual report. The Nov 3, 2026 ballot includes the statewide school tax-cap question (HB 1300).

            Known gaps and conflicts

            Where sources disagree and what could not be found, so you know what to double-check.

            In plain language

            No source is perfect. Check these items before relying on them. Current as of Oct 9, 2026.

            Conflicts between sources

            Conflict
            Forristall Rd variance (Case 2026-12). The ZBA's Sept 22 draft minutes show the variance granted 4-1. On Oct 7 the Select Board voted 3-0 to request a rehearing (from meeting audio; unofficial). Neither the ZBA nor the Select Board has posted a record of the request yet.
            Conflict
            Default budget amount. The official warrant gives $5,654,177. The Ledger-Transcript reported $5.64M (and $5.65M in January); the Keene Sentinel reported $5.7M. This site uses the warrant figure.
            Conflict
            Draft vs. final 2026 warrant. The Jan 7 draft had a $25,000 Revaluation CRF (pulled Jan 21), a $150,000 Highway CRF (the final article was $185,000), a Land Use Change Tax share of 20% (amended to 99% at the Deliberative Session), and different article numbers (the veterans' credit was Art. 11 in the draft and Art. 12 on the final warrant).
            Conflict
            Deliberative Session timing. The Town Clerk's elections page describes the session as typically the first Saturday of February, but the 2026 session was Sat Jan 31, the earliest legal date. The 2027 date (between Jan 30 and Feb 6) has not been posted.
            Conflict
            Petition deadline. The general RSA 39:3 "fifth Tuesday" rule would give Feb 2, 2027, but SB2 towns follow RSA 40:13: the second Tuesday in January (Jan 12, 2027). The town has not posted this date.
            Conflict
            Election results source. The town's results page (news item T2_R44) returned 404 on Oct 9. The Ledger-Transcript and Keene Sentinel report the same tallies; the Sentinel lists the budget as 824-707 (no-yes).
            Conflict
            Conservation Commission position on 75 ft. "Opposes" appears only in an automated summary. Official minutes show concerns and a consultant review, but no vote or position.
            Conflict
            2023 and 2024 budget tallies. The 2023 and 2024 annual reports both print 497-256 for the operating budget, and 2024 Articles 5 and 9 (zoning Amendments 4 and 8) both print 666-237. These tallies are withheld here until the Town Clerk confirms them.
            Conflict
            2018 Article 13 (250th Anniversary trust fund). Unresolved. The typed minutes show a 715-715 tie (a tie fails), but a handwritten recount note on the ballot page reads 711-707. Later records show the fund existed.
            Conflict
            Elderly married income limit. The 2025 MS-1 report prints $49,000 (the figure set by the 2012 petition); the 2020 MS-1 printed $50,000. Single ($35,000) and asset ($150,000) limits match.
            Conflict
            2021 elderly exemption article. The 2021 report prints the original Article 19 wording (lowering the limits). The Deliberative Session had amended it into a study committee, and the 748-376 vote was on the study article.
            Conflict
            2023 zoning vote date. The 2023 report gives March 14, 2023; the Wetlands Ordinance cover and the amendment list say March 28, 2023.
            Conflict
            2016 Deliberative Session date. The 2016 report (scan) says Sat Jan 30, 2016; an unofficial copy of the minutes says Sat Feb 6, 2016.
            Conflict
            2025 default budget. Select Board minutes and the 2025 report give $5,487,882; the Ledger-Transcript reported $4.49M. The Select Board later found errors and filed an amended default (Nov 12, 2025).
            Conflict
            2025 revaluation increase. The town's reassessment page gives an average residential increase of 89.6%; Select Board minutes cite about 96.7%. They may measure different things.

            Gaps: not found or not posted

            Gap
            Select Board minutes not posted: Apr 15, Apr 22, May 6, Aug 26, Sept 9, Sept 23, Oct 7. The Mar 25 minutes link does not open a PDF.
            Gap
            Planning Board minutes for Sept 1 and Oct 6 not yet approved; no subcommittee minutes after Apr 6. No recording of the Oct 6 meeting was found.
            Gap
            Conservation Commission minutes for Aug 27 and Sept 24 not posted; Sept 24 and Oct 12 outcomes unknown. The LEC review report itself was not found.
            Gap
            Budget Advisory Committee: no 2026 minutes posted. A joint Select Board/BAC FY28 budget meeting (Sept 22 or 28; sources disagree) has no official agenda or minutes, and its recording was not reviewed.
            Gap
            Non-public sessions are not recorded or summarized.
            Gap
            School district: agendas, minutes, enrollment and budget figures not reviewed.
            Gap
            No March 2027 zoning amendment text or hearing notice posted.
            Gap
            No Rindge-posted 2027 election calendar, petition deadline or Deliberative Session date.
            Gap
            The town's official 2026 election results page returned 404 on Oct 9, so election tallies here are press-reported. Tallies for Articles 12-14 were not found.
            Gap
            Several approved ZBA minutes are image scans; the text of the corresponding draft minutes was used. Case 2026-05 was not located.
            Gap
            Sept 9, Sept 23 and Oct 7 Select Board items come from machine speech-to-text of the meeting audio; names, amounts and outcomes are approximate until minutes are posted.
            Gap
            The Wetlands Conservation District Ordinance file is dated 2023; later amendments were not confirmed.
            Gap
            The town ZBA index also lists 2024-2025 documents with ambiguous dates; only 2026-folder documents are shown here.
            Gap
            The town's online agendas and minutes start in Sept 2024. Older minutes need a records request to the Executive Secretary or Town Administrator, so any "first found" date before Sept 2024 comes from annual reports or press and is an upper bound.
            Gap
            Annual reports for 2011–2014, 2016 and 2021 are scans. Tallies read from them are marked "scan, verify against PDF". 2018 zoning tallies are cropped in the scan, and illegible digits are not shown.
            Gap
            March 2026 results are not in any annual report yet; the 2026 figures on this site are press-reported.
            Gap
            Turnout for 2021–2026 and elderly exemption totals for 2016 and 2021–2024 were not found.

            Report a correction
